title: Adobe Photoshop & Lightroom Production Core v1

domain.name: Adobe Photoshop & Lightroom Production
domain.description: Professional photo organization, raw development, masking, retouching, compositing, color, batch workflow, and delivery across Lightroom and Photoshop.

competencies.name: Catalogs, Files & Non-Destructive Workflow
competencies.description: Manage originals, catalogs, sidecars, edits, and exports without losing provenance.
competencies.purpose: Keep photo projects recoverable and easy to revisit.

units.title: Catalog data is not the original image
units.content: Ratings, edits, virtual copies, and organization metadata may live separately from source files; backup strategy must cover both.

units.title: Photo ingest workflow
units.content: Copy originals to verified storage; preserve camera filenames or apply a documented rename; create catalog/project structure; add metadata; back up before culling; keep exports separate from originals.

units.title: Catalog workflow failures
units.content: Avoid moving files outside the catalog without relinking, confusing previews with originals, destructive overwrites, and assuming one catalog backup protects source photos.

drills.title: Design a wedding photo ingest plan
drills.prompt: Plan primary copy, backup, catalog structure, naming, and verification for a multi-card event.

competencies.name: RAW Development & Global Correction
competencies.description: Use raw controls to establish exposure, white balance, tone, color, and lens correction.
competencies.purpose: Create a technically strong base before local retouching or stylization.

units.title: Raw development order
units.content: Confirm profile and white balance; set exposure and highlight/shadow relationships; correct obvious lens issues; shape global contrast; refine color; then use local masks for scene-specific adjustments.

units.title: Solve global problems globally first
units.content: Do not build dozens of local masks to fix a wrong exposure or white balance that affects the whole frame.

units.title: Raw development failures
units.content: Avoid clipping important channels, excessive clarity/texture, correcting skin with global saturation, and using auto settings without reviewing consistency across a set.

drills.title: Match a mixed-light photo set
drills.prompt: Plan a raw workflow for indoor/outdoor images that need a cohesive event gallery.
rubric: Local masks reserved for local problems

competencies.name: Culling, Rating & Selection
competencies.description: Select images using technical quality, expression, storytelling, redundancy, and client needs.
competencies.purpose: Reduce large shoots without losing important moments or variety.

units.title: Multi-pass cull
units.content: First remove unusable technical failures; then choose strongest expressions and moments; then reduce near-duplicates; finally check story coverage, key people, and required deliverables.

units.title: Cull for the final story, not isolated perfection
units.content: A slightly imperfect frame can matter if it carries the only meaningful moment; selection is a set-level decision.

units.title: Culling failures
units.content: Avoid choosing only technically perfect images, keeping every near-duplicate, deleting before backup, and ignoring requested people or event milestones.

drills.title: Cull a 500-image event
drills.prompt: Define passes and decision rules for reducing a large event while preserving coverage.

competencies.name: Masking & Local Adjustments
competencies.description: Use subject, luminance, color, gradient, and brush masks to shape attention and correct localized problems.
competencies.purpose: Refine images without flattening natural light and texture.

units.title: Masks should follow image structure
units.content: Local adjustments work best when boundaries, depth, light direction, and material behavior support the change.

units.title: Local adjustment workflow
units.content: Define the visual problem; choose the simplest mask type; refine edge/feather; make the minimum tonal/color change needed; inspect at fit view and 100%; verify consistency with neighboring images.

units.title: Masking failures
units.content: Avoid halos around subjects, over-bright faces detached from scene light, excessive skin texture removal, and stacking masks that fight each other.

drills.title: Refine a portrait with local masks
drills.prompt: Plan subject, background, skin, and eye adjustments while keeping the portrait natural.

competencies.name: Photoshop Retouching & Cleanup
competencies.description: Remove distractions and repair detail with cloning, healing, frequency-aware judgment, and reversible layers.
competencies.purpose: Perform high-quality cleanup without creating synthetic artifacts.

units.title: Retouch workflow
units.content: Duplicate or create repair layers; choose healing for texture-aware fixes and cloning where exact source control is needed; work at appropriate zoom; preserve natural repeating texture; toggle layers often; inspect at final output size.

units.title: Retouch to remove the distraction, not the evidence of reality
units.content: Natural skin, fabric, architecture, and backgrounds need texture and variation; perfect smoothness usually looks fake.

units.title: Retouch failures
units.content: Avoid repeated clone patterns, blurred skin, mismatched grain, warped straight lines, and flattening before review.

drills.title: Retouch a distracting event photo
drills.prompt: Plan removal of background distractions and minor skin cleanup with reversible edits.

competencies.name: Photoshop Compositing & Selection
competencies.description: Combine images using selections, masks, transforms, perspective, lighting, and edge integration.
competencies.purpose: Create believable still composites and advanced corrections.

units.title: Composite workflow
units.content: Choose compatible sources; align scale and perspective; create clean masks; match light direction and contrast; match color and depth of field; add contact shadows/reflections when physically needed; finish with unified grain/sharpening.

units.title: Composite failures
units.content: Avoid perfect cutout edges, inconsistent perspective, missing contact shadows, conflicting color temperature, and sharpening elements differently from the base image.

units.title: Geometry before color
units.content: A composite with wrong perspective or scale cannot be rescued by color grading; solve structure first.

drills.title: Build a group-photo composite plan
drills.prompt: Describe how to replace one person's expression from a nearby frame without visible seams.

competencies.name: Color Management, Soft Proofing & Print Awareness
competencies.description: Understand profiles, working spaces, display conditions, and output intent.
competencies.purpose: Reduce surprises between editing, web delivery, and print.

units.title: Color appearance depends on interpretation
units.content: Numeric RGB values only make sense when paired with a color space/profile and viewed through a managed display/output pipeline.

units.title: Output color workflow
units.content: Keep source/profile information intact; edit in an appropriate managed space; soft proof when print/output profile is known; evaluate gamut warnings as guidance; export using the target's required profile and bit depth.

units.title: Color management failures
units.content: Avoid assigning versus converting profiles accidentally, stripping profiles without reason, judging print solely from a bright monitor, and applying display compensation into the image file.

drills.title: Prepare an image for print and web
drills.prompt: Plan separate outputs from one master edit, including profile and proofing decisions.

competencies.name: Batch Editing, Sync & Delivery
competencies.description: Apply repeatable edits across sets while preserving image-specific exceptions.
competencies.purpose: Deliver large galleries efficiently and consistently.

units.title: Batch workflow
units.content: Develop representative anchor images; synchronize only parameters that truly generalize; review exceptions; apply crop/straightening individually when needed; export named derivatives into separate destinations; verify a sample across the set.

units.title: Sync intent, not blind settings
units.content: A synchronized exposure value may be wrong across changing light; synchronize the correction logic only where image conditions are comparable.

units.title: Batch failures
units.content: Avoid syncing local masks to incompatible compositions, overwriting originals, exporting mixed color spaces unexpectedly, and assuming a successful batch means every file is correct.

drills.title: Prepare a client gallery batch
drills.prompt: Create a batch workflow for a large event gallery with web JPEGs, social crops, and archive masters.
